thread:
infra-bot: ALERT: High rate of GPU driver Xid errors (Xid 31/43) observed in pool 'inference-gpu-prd' starting at 18:47 UTC. 320 events in last 10m. Affected nodes: gpu-n1-12,gpu-n1-15,gpu-n1-18. Auto-evacuation triggered for 2 nodes. Links: https://telemetry.redwood/inference-gpu-prd/errors?range=10m :rotating_light:

james (oncall): seeing dashboard. latency spike + 502s on a few routes. Are customers currently affected?

priya (sre): yes, a handful of inference requests are returning 5xx from runtime container restarts. Alert shows correctable ECC + Xid 31 entries in dmesg on gpu-n1-15. Posting snippet:

priya (sre): ```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=23456, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679002] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.680123] kernel: Device 0000:65:00.0: reported EFER: ECC corrected error
```

leo (infra): thanks — that matches nv-host logs. temp and ECC counters ticked up before the resets. Running `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Running` shows a few pods constantly restarting on those nodes.

james (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) cordon gpu-n1-15 and gpu-n1-18, 2) drain non-critical pods, 3) spin up cpu-fallback replicas for critical routes, 4) open customer bridge for impacted customers and set regen model fallback. Any objections? :thumbsup:

emma (cust-eng): please open bridge — customers A and C are on the high-priority list, they saw increased latency. I'll start outreach.

priya (sre): executing cordon/drain now. command: `kubectl cordon gpu-n1-15 && kubectl drain gpu-n1-15 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m`

ops-bot: ACTION: cordon and drain started by priya (sre) at 18:55 UTC. Evac status: pod eviction in progress.

leo (infra): quick debug checklist I'm running in parallel:
- ssh to node -> `dmesg | tail -n 200`
- `nvidia-smi -q` for ECC counters and processes
- check kernel oops in /var/log/kern.log
- capture container logs `docker logs --since 10m <container>`

priya (sre): got full dmesg, pushed to gist: https://gist.redwood/dmesg-gpu-n1-15. Key lines show repeated `Xid 31` followed by `nvidia-motherboard: wdog reset` then container OOM-like restarts.

james (oncall): can we try a driver reload on a quarantined node or should we prefer reboot? Past incidents had kernel oops after modprobe -r.

leo (infra): try `systemctl restart nvidia-docker` first, if Xid still recurs, schedule a node reboot. If kernel oops present, go straight to reboot. I'll attempt restart on gpu-n1-12 (non-evacuated) to test.

leo (infra): attempted `systemctl restart nvidia-docker` on gpu-n1-12 — logs show quick driver unload then load, no immediate Xid. Monitoring.

priya (sre): drain on gpu-n1-15 completed. Non-critical replicas moved. Critical routes are hitting cpu-fallback pool. Confirming no new 5xx for routes routed to fallback.

emma (cust-eng): customers A/C confirmed degraded but not failing; appreciate the quick fallback. I'll hold bridge update until we know reboot plan.

james (oncall): update: cpu-fallback is stable. Still seeing Xid noise on gpu-n1-18 in telemetry. Decision: reboot gpu-n1-18 after demotion. Priya — can you annotate impacted pods and schedule reboot?

priya (sre): scheduling reboot via `/usr/local/bin/node-reboot --node gpu-n1-18 --reason "Xid spike/ECC corrections" --drain-timeout 2m` now. ETA ~ 3m for reboot to start.

ops-bot: NOTE: Node gpu-n1-18 entered reboot workflow at 19:03 UTC.

leo (infra): collecting nv-host logs pre-reboot for RCA. Found parity ECC corrections at approx 19:01 UTC, then Xid 43 on PCI:0000:66:00. Attaching short snippet:

leo (infra): ```
[  19:01:02] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:66:00): 43, pid=45678, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  19:01:03] kernel: ecc: corrected error on gpu 66 count=3
```

james (oncall): customer bridge now live. Emma on the bridge. Notifying SLA owners.

emma (cust-eng): bridge note: "We're seeing intermittent driver resets on a subset of GPU hosts. Failover to CPU is active for critical traffic. CS is monitoring and will update customers every 30m or on material changes."

priya (sre): reboot complete on gpu-n1-18, node back in cluster and cordon removed. Post-reboot telemetry shows reduced Xid events but still some ECC corrections on gpu-n1-12.

leo (infra): next steps: 1) run overnight soak on gpu-n1-12 with increased ECC logging, 2) schedule firmware/driver bump to latest validated build in canary cluster, 3) set temporary kube label `gpu.stability=degraded` to avoid scheduling high-throughput jobs. I'll open infra ticket and link here.

james (oncall): handoff to priya for follow-up and RCA. Key items for next oncall: continue soak, coordinate driver/firmware rollout with platform repo, and validate fallback routing remains healthy. Priya — take over? :white_check_mark:

priya (sre): taking the handoff. Summary for next oncall: - Impact: transient 5xx on inference routes due to GPU driver Xid resets and ECC corrections on 3 nodes. - Mitigation: cordon/drain + cpu-fallback + node reboot for two nodes. - Status: customer bridge open, cpu-fallback active, one node (gpu-n1-12) under observation. - Action items: run extended telemetry, run driver firmware upgrade in canary, follow-up with HW vendor if ECC persists.

james (oncall): thanks all — leaving notes in incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood/3187654000. I'm out for the shift. Priya will be primary. :wave:
